Routine start working rules for noise levels
This page shows new staff what is expected

The Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways helps keep animal travel calm, safe, and respectful for everyone in the terminal. Noise control matters because frightened pets, worried travelers, and busy staff all do better when the desk stays steady and quiet. Your voice, pace, and body language all shape the experience, so start each interaction by making the space feel settled.

When a traveler arrives, greet them in a low, even tone and keep your instructions simple. If the area is busy, step closer rather than raising your voice, and keep radio chatter and side talk to a minimum. You are helping passengers understand the process without adding stress, and that includes the animal on the other side of the carrier. <<FACT F067>> Keep your attention on the traveler, the pet, and the paperwork together so nothing feels rushed.

Use calm language when you explain checks, crate handling, and document review. If a pet is vocal, do not answer with sudden movements or sharp sounds. Instead, lower your own energy, give the animal space, and let the traveler know what you are doing before you do it. A steady approach helps prevent a small worry from becoming a bigger problem.

If you need support from another staff member, signal quietly and speak only as much as needed. Avoid calling across the desk or talking over the traveler. Clear, quiet communication protects the line flow and shows passengers that we are in control of the situation. If a pet seems distressed, pause, observe, and bring in the senior coordinator according to local procedure.

Remember that companion animal care is part of the whole travel experience, not a side task. Every polite word, gentle gesture, and quiet check builds trust in Aurelia Skyways and keeps the desk running smoothly. What to remember is simple: stay calm, speak softly, and make every animal feel handled with care.
